issues.description: Inconsistent method naming for the meal price calculation: the problem specification and UML require a method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int, but the solution implements a static method named computeMealCost(Meal) while the solution's Main still calls calculateTotalPrice. The template Main also references computeMealCost. This name/signature mismatch across artifacts can confuse students about the required method name and cause compilation errors when following example code.
issues.suggestedFix: Pick a single method name for the meal price calculation and use it consistently. Rename the method in SealSaloon to calculateTotalPrice(Meal): int (and keep it static), or update all example Main usage and documentation to call computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure the template, problem text, and solution use the same name.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's cost, but the solution implements this functionality as a static method named computeMealCost(Meal). Additionally, the solution's Main (commented) calls calculateTotalPrice while SealSaloon defines computeMealCost. This name divergence for the same conceptual operation (computing total price of a Meal) creates unnecessary mapping confusion for students.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent method name across artifacts. Rename the solution method computeMealCost(Meal) to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (keeping it static and returning int), and update any calls (e.g., in Main) to calculateTotalPrice so names match the problem statement and UML.
